name: Cellular democracy
summary: Cellular democracy is Fred Foldvary's proposal to replace mass elections with bottom-up voting: residents elect small neighborhood councils, and each level of council sends delegates to the next level up. Because voters can meet candidates face to face, special-interest campaign money and rent-seeking are meant to lose their payoff. Foldvary pairs it with voluntary, contractual communities, secession and service substitution rights, and revenue that flows upward from site rents.
scope: The model as set out by Fred Foldvary (1997 onward, the 2002 Review of Austrian Economics article, the 2015 essay 'Radical Democracy' and the Foldvary and Minola paper in Cosmos+Taxis, 2020) within geolibertarian, public-choice thinking. It excludes other uses of 'cell' or 'ward' democracy and answers on the many unrelated questions by inference from his geolibertarian outlook, so most answers outside governance structure, finance and consent are low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Foldvary's papers cover local public goods financed from site rents but never address healthcare; adherents could fund it locally or leave it to contract, so the lane is split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The paper wants market-based spontaneous planning and cites Hayek's knowledge problem against central direction, though public goods remain collectively provided.

public-ownership.rationale: Foldvary favors private or neighborhood-controlled provision of streets and utilities and decentralized councils over central state ownership of industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He rejects forced redistribution as a superficial remedy to poverty and wants revenue from land rent instead of income taxes, so higher taxes on the wealthy are not a goal.

unions-good.rationale: The paper cites union bottom-up elections as an example of multi-level voting but takes no stand on unions' worth to workers or society.

property-fundamental.rationale: Geolibertarians protect private property in improvements but treat land rent as a common fund, so a very hard-to-override property right splits the position.

strong-leader.rationale: He argues that concentrated power invites rent-seeking and that decentralization is the remedy, so a leader bypassing checks is contrary to the model.

state-harmful.rationale: He keeps governance, as nested councils, but wants it small, voluntary and bottom-up, so he rejects having no state at all while limiting its scale.

decide-locally.rationale: The paper's central claim is that governance should be devolved to small neighborhood councils, citing Buchanan and Tullock that collective activity belongs in small rather than large units.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He offers secession for a discriminated minority to form its own council but proposes no active corrective policy.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The paper values communities choosing their own cultures through mobility but takes no national-culture stance.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: His preference for decentralization and small-unit governance runs against giving remote international bodies more power, though he notes UN delegates are chosen indirectly.

open-borders.rationale: He values mobility between communities but he also treats membership as contractual; open national borders are never addressed.

limit-growth.rationale: He backs a green tax shift that strengthens the economy, not limiting growth as such.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): the old wording asked whether revolution is sometimes justified, and this disagreement rested on a preference for reform or lawful means, which doesn't say revolution is never justified.

reviewHistory.rationale: He proposes reform through conversion of one legislative chamber and bottom-up voting, not revolution.

central-planning.rationale: The paper argues spontaneous, decentralized planning using local tacit knowledge beats master plans, citing Hayek's knowledge problem.

land-value-tax.rationale: The paper concludes that community competition would make site rents the basic public revenue and Foldvary is a Georgist who favors land value tax as the least intrusive source.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He opposes general taxes and favors land rent; heavy inheritance taxes are not part of his revenue scheme.

basic-income.rationale: Georgists often propose a rent dividend, but Foldvary's sources here do not; he also calls forced redistribution superficial, so split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He cites Tullock on tariffs as welfare-wasting transfers and condemns protection from competition as economic rents.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He condemns subsidies and privileges as economic rents and favors spontaneous order, so state-directed investment is contrary.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: His model rests on market-based planning, rents and prices; abolishing money and wage labor contradicts it entirely.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies fixing wages and prices are the kind of centralized privilege he blames on special interests.

one-party-rule.rationale: He wants small face-to-face voting that limits party and special-interest power, and criticizes the Soviet party's top-down control.

democracy-best.rationale: He defends democracy, calling it absolute only with consent and agreeing with Churchill's formula while insisting its structure must be reformed.

direct-votes.rationale: He stresses that citizens vote only for neighborhood councils, which choose delegates upward, rather than voting on laws directly.

workers-councils.rationale: He borrows the anarchist and soviet multi-level idea but bases councils on residential neighborhoods, not workplaces, and criticizes Soviet practice.

right-to-secede.rationale: The paper lets any council secede from the next level and lets landowners withdraw property from government jurisdiction, with possible exit fees.

natural-rulers.rationale: His starting point is individual sovereignty among equals, which excludes natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: He holds that majorities impose by force on minorities, but he does not address whether political violence is ever justified.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Without consent from everyone bound, scripture-based law would be imposition on his terms, though communities may adopt rules by contract.

private-courts-defense.rationale: He champions private contractual communities and argues against the idea of market failure in public goods, though his model keeps nested public councils.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He explains conflict through rent-seeking by special interests rather than class struggle, and treats forced redistribution as superficial.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He cites Weber that formal equality fails the propertyless but dismisses forced redistribution; he seeks equal access to land rent, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: He proposed paying rent for occupied land to resolve territorial conflict, which is neither agreement nor rejection of indigenous authority.

civilizational-union.rationale: His small-unit decentralism opposes consolidating nations into larger political unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He builds institutions around self-interested actors but also holds a universal ethic; the sources don't call self-interest morally good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He begins with individual sovereignty and rights and says a constitution protects liberty, so duties do not outrank rights.

restore-past-order.rationale: He proposes a new institutional design, not a restoration, though he draws on Howard's garden cities and anarchist federalism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: His method is institutional and theory-driven public choice analysis, but he does not argue against ideology.

direct-action.rationale: He seeks reform via constitutional change, converting a legislative chamber and a mass movement, not direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: He insists that governance be consensual and voluntary, implying means should reflect ends, but states no general principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: He favors markets, cities with rents and spontaneous order; a hunter-gatherer return is absent from and contrary to his work.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: He relies on Hayek's decentralized, specialized knowledge and market production, so abolishing division of labor contradicts his analysis.

distribute-by-need.rationale: He is skeptical of forced redistribution and relies on rents and contract, rejecting need-based distribution as the principle.

production-for-use.rationale: He favors market competition where firms profit by pleasing customers, not production for use alone.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He locates exploitation in economic rents and privileges, not in profit from owning businesses.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He criticizes Communist Party top-down control of the soviets and wants consensual bottom-up rule, not class dictatorship.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He blames rent-seeking and imposed force by states rather than capitalism; war causation is not directly discussed.

taxation-theft.rationale: He proposes taxes, chiefly site rents, and sees them as legitimate public revenue though he criticizes coercive mass-democratic imposition.

individual-rights-only.rationale: He starts from individual sovereignty and a contract among equal sovereigns, with a constitution protecting liberty from majority tyranny.

exit-over-voice.rationale: He pairs exit with voice, saying the exit option supplements the voice option, so neither is ranked clearly above the other.

state-as-business.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value turns on whether citizens are customers who can leave, and the statement now asks only whether government should be run on business principles.

reviewHistory.rationale: He treats communities as competing providers whose residents can leave or secede, close to the customer analogy, with rent-based fees.

positive-liberty.rationale: He emphasizes individual sovereignty and freedom from imposition and calls forced redistribution superficial, so material-means-based freedom is not central.

media-academia-power.rationale: His analysis puts power with special interests funding mass campaigns, not universities and media.

organic-representation.rationale: Residential neighborhood councils sending delegates upward resemble local-community representation, but not family or trade bodies.

total-state.rationale: The model devolves power to small councils and voluntary contractual communities and criticizes centralization, explicitly opposed to state direction of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Radical national rebirth has no place in his institutional, reformist public-choice argument.

territorial-expansion.rationale: His territorial-conflict proposals use confederation and rent payments, not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority by consent of equal sovereigns excludes rule by personal oaths.

universal-morality.rationale: Wikipedia lists his universal ethic as a central writing theme, implying universal moral truths.

single-common-good.rationale: He builds competition among communities with different mixes of fees and services, accepting plural preferences over a single good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: None of the sources read discuss Zionism or Israel; Foldvary's territorial proposals (confederation, rent for occupied land) do not settle it, so neutral.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Return rights for diasporas never come up in the cellular democracy papers; his mobility-friendly stance gives no firm lean, so neutral.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is outside a model about nested neighborhood councils, and nothing read gives a view, so the answer is neutral.

school-vouchers.rationale: He proposes service substitution so councils can run their own schools and deduct costs, and favors choice and competition; vouchers not mentioned.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: His papers deal with local site-rent finance and not macro stimulus; adherents could go either way, so neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: Described as advocating free markets and civil liberties together, implying they go together.

rule-by-example.rationale: His model relies on institutional incentives and constitutional constraints rather than rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: He supports secession and self-governing groups, which is close to self-determination, though he stresses councils not nations.

force-without-un.rationale: The sources never touch on use of force abroad or the UN Security Council, leaving no basis for a lean.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He uses economic reasoning but takes no stance on faith versus reason.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He criticizes forced redistribution but never discusses work requirements.

workers-nation.rationale: Organizing the working class by nation or internationally is a Marxist question outside his model of residential councils.

ban-interest.rationale: He favors market institutions and land rent; banning lending at interest is outside and contrary to his analysis.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He proposes secession for discriminated minorities and universal ethic; legal racial separation imposed by law contradicts consent.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He sees the state as captured by special interests seeking rents, which is related but not a class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He supports pollution charges and royalties from extraction rents, neither expansion nor restriction.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Communities set own culture through contract and mobility; compulsory assimilation is not part of it.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy about elites replacing populations has no support in his public-choice account.

proportional-representation.rationale: He criticizes the party model of mass democracy and prefers geographic bottom-up councils.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a form of government by mission conflicts with his emphasis on consent and local choice.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: His public-choice analysis argues special-interest funding leads officials to reward transfers and privileges.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He keeps public goods provided by councils funded by rents, which is broader than a night-watchman role, but small in scale.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Individual sovereignty and universal ethic reject state discouragement of marriage by race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He holds individuals are equal sovereigns who contract with each other, supporting equal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The statement belongs to Marxist debates that his geolibertarian model does not engage, so neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: He proposed paying rent for occupied land to defuse territorial conflict but never characterizes settler states, so neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: It would violate individual sovereignty and consent.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: He wants state power devolved and weakened, not strengthened.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He argues that absolute democracy requires each participant's voluntary agreement and signed consent, and that an unsigned constitution lacks legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: He cites Tullock against tariffs; mercantilist surplus targets are not part of his view.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal contradicts consent and individual sovereignty.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He objects that majorities impose their will by force on minorities; his universal ethic supports this, though taxes remain.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about competition between individuals or in markets, and this statement now asks only about struggle between peoples.

reviewHistory.rationale: He treats competition between communities as a driver of efficiency, but not between peoples as struggle.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about competition between individuals or in markets, and this statement now asks only about struggle between peoples.

separated-powers.rationale: He discusses federalism and branches as constitutional constraints and adds cellular democracy to limit power further.

vanguard-party.rationale: He criticizes Communist control and favors voluntary bottom-up organization.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He wants to end privileges that cause poverty but rejects forced redistribution; no explicit priority.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He attributes poverty to rents and privileges rather than population, in Georgist fashion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: He designs elections of councils by neighbors who know candidates, not lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He wants a constitution protecting liberty from majorities; suspending protections contradicts that.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: He favors market allocation and decries state-privilege interventions.

party-controls-media.rationale: Civil liberties and anti-central control; criticizes mass media money.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army conflicts with decentralizing power.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Prefers decentralization, though he notes multi-level structures could extend worldwide through bottom-up councils.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Council-chosen executive: legislature elects the governor under his transition plan, so legislature-chosen heads are favored.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority by consent of equal sovereigns excludes clerical rule.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: His model depends on rental value and leaseholds, citing Howard's leasehold model.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: His analysis favors dense, rent-maximizing compact cities, avoiding sprawl.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not mentioned in the sources; adherents' civil-libertarian and consent-based premises point both ways, so neutral.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: His model has voluntary membership by contract, not descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-10): its rationale records no position; silence is not a position, so the sources cited here do not answer this statement.

reviewHistory.rationale: Language policy appears nowhere in the sources; local councils would decide, so neutral.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Post-colonial economics is outside his writing on local councils, so neutral.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He says a constitution requires real consent, but not a constituent assembly specifically.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: He links civil liberties to free markets; sacrificing them contradicts that.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Under cellular democracy, the president is elected by Congress or a legislature elected from below, not directly.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He proposed rent payments and confederations for territorial conflict, a compromise-oriented stance, but no direct statement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Georgist view: land rent belongs to the community, but improvements are private; split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He notes the Soviets became top-down party rule but does not characterize the economy.

precautionary-principle.rationale: He supports pollution charges but does not discuss acting under scientific uncertainty, so neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance commitments like NATO's Article 5 are mentioned only as examples of indirectly chosen delegates, so neutral.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The papers have the legislature elect the executive but do not discuss a ceremonial nonpartisan head, so neutral.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He explicitly allows councils to secede, so preventing it by force is incompatible with his model.

region-keeps-system.rationale: His model lets communities choose their own revenue source and services even within a larger structure, and lets them partially withdraw.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Equal sovereigns by consent exclude sacred rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: He wants no general income taxes at all, relying on site rents, so a flat income tax is not his aim.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He holds that a constitution must protect liberty and bind governors, with consent as basis for legitimacy.

space-expansion.rationale: Spaceflight is outside his writings, so neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: He combines bottom-up councils with constitutional limits but does not argue mixing few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Reducing the personality-driven mass media dynamic is his aim; leader cult is contrary.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism that his model does not engage, so neutral.

land-redistribution.rationale: Georgists tax land rent rather than seize estates; land-value taxation, not redistribution of holdings, is his remedy.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims on nationality conflict with consent-based governance.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing a person for leaving a religion would override the individual sovereignty and consent that anchor his theory of legitimate governance.

women-must-cover.rationale: Imposes dress by law on individuals, contrary to individual sovereignty.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Self-governing groups choose own institutions; close to his secession-based proposal, but unlabelled.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: He proposes secession for discriminated minorities but also mobility; split.

ban-cartels.rationale: He opposes privileges and protection from competition, which could support anti-cartel action, but he distrusts central regulation, so split toward no.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He wants a constitution protecting liberty from majorities, so courts constraining majority rule is accepted.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: His free-trade, mobility and market leanings run against bloc self-sufficiency.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: He backs pollution charges but nothing on binding trade-agreement standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: His analysis builds on material incentives, such as rent-based payments and competition.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He seeks reform by constitutional conversion, not armed vanguards.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule over others without consent contradicts his consent doctrine.

patriotic-education.rationale: Councils decide schooling locally and he offers no support for state-mandated patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: He opposes privileges but is silent on admissions preferences.

delink-world-market.rationale: He favors mobility of goods and people, not breaking economic ties.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He says a constitution is needed to protect liberty from majority tyranny, if consented to.

elective-rulers.rationale: His cellular model is entirely elected, from neighborhood councils upward.

minority-veto.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on a group veto or on the difference between a veto and exit, and the statement now asks whether a decision should bind only those who consent to it.

reviewHistory.rationale: He wants consent of every member to the contract and an exit option rather than a veto on each decision, so he sits between.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He prefers limiting any single body via division of powers and councils.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He rejects forced redistribution but never discusses voluntary duties of the wealthy, so neutral.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: His cellular model relies on engaged neighborhood participation, with face-to-face meetings.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: He criticizes mass media for campaign dynamics, not for pacifying people.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: He blames special-interest funding; he does not use hegemony theory.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: His framework attributes poverty to local rents and privileges, not world-system extraction.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: His writing opposes slavery; not directly addressed here.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He holds universal ethic; proposes cellular democracy as broadly applicable, even worldwide.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Armed forces ruling contradicts consent and elected representation.

office-by-exam.rationale: His model fills offices by election from below, not exam.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Georgist view that land rent belongs to the community is shown in his site-rent funding, while buildings stay private; leasehold model cited from Howard.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Councils fund each level from below, implying legislative control of finances.

corporate-influence.rationale: He argues special interests supply campaign funds to candidates and reap transfers, which cellular democracy reduces.

job-guarantee.rationale: State-guaranteed jobs are a transfer and conflict with his market and anti-redistribution views.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Obligation arises from consent; without it, no duty, but he does not state this directly.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims have no basis in his analysis.

local-production.rationale: He opposes centralized planning but supports mobility and markets, so local production as a goal is not his.

informal-organisation.rationale: He favors formal councils, not informal groups.

religious-nation.rationale: Excludes by consent and individual sovereignty.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Foreign deference to a great power contradicts his emphasis on consent and decentralized, self-governing units.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: He proposes revenue starting at level 1 and flowing upward, with each level funded by the one below and no general taxes on lower levels.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: His site-rent system taxes land but leaves improvements and other property private, supporting private possessions.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: He proposes service substitution and private communities alongside public provision.

cooperative-communities.rationale: He proposes voluntary contractual neighborhood communities networked by councils, similar to small self-governing communities though not cooperatives.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Criminalizing private adult conduct conflicts with the individual sovereignty and civil liberties his theory rests on.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He argues for consent and absolute democracy with liberty protected by constitution, contrary to suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Punishing speech about religion conflicts with the individual sovereignty and civil liberties at the base of his theory.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Rule without consent contradicts his doctrine.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious-law question outside his political model, so neutral.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Declaring rulers illegitimate for not following religious law conflicts with his consent-based, secular basis of authority.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Small-group voting lets every person participate and meet candidates, though only for neighborhood councils.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He grounds authority in each person's consent among equal sovereigns, not divine delegation.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Contradicts elected councils and equal sovereignty.

property-franchise.rationale: Equal sovereigns each vote in neighborhood cells.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-Lukacsian concept outside his work, so neutral.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: He does criticize money in politics but not press ownership.

online-participation.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about online deliberation, consultation or political participation in general, not voting, and the statement now asks whether citizens should have the option to vote online in public elections.

reviewHistory.rationale: He stresses face-to-face meetings, so online-only deliberation is not his model.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Legal limits on whom one may marry contradict the individual sovereignty at his theory's base. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not lottery; elected councils, though both small-group deliberation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He worries about special-interest funding, not wealth concentration as such.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State promotion of a belief contradicts his consent-based theory of legitimate government.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He enables secession for minorities rather than guaranteed sharing.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious internal governance is outside his political writing, so neutral.

rent-control.rationale: He favors market pricing of rent and site rent as revenue.

uniformed-youth.rationale: State-organized youth movements contradict his consent-based, voluntary approach to association.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Georgists favor earned income and public land rent.

god-not-male.rationale: Theological language is outside his political writing, so neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Theological hermeneutics are outside his political writing, so neutral.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Contradicts equal sovereignty and free markets.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A Marxist criterion that his geolibertarian model does not engage, so neutral.

municipal-property.rationale: Land rent goes to community councils but buildings private; split.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Multi-level councils with delegates sent upward, plus confederation proposals, resemble confederal coordination.

person-over-state.rationale: Individual sovereignty is his starting point.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Metaphysical claim outside his political writing, so neutral.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Powers flow upward from level-1 councils, and higher levels cannot tax lower ones; regions' powers are not granted at will from above.

dense-cities.rationale: He argues rent-based finance induces compact structures that prevent sprawl and blight.

communal-electorates.rationale: Voters elect neighborhood councils on a territorial basis as equals, not by religious community, so communal electorates are inconsistent.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on whether a foreign plot is believed to exist, or on foreign hostility in general rather than territorial partition, and the statement now asks whether preventing foreign-backed partition should be a central aim of national policy.

reviewHistory.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in his analysis, which blames domestic special-interest rent seeking.

reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

capital-controls.rationale: He favors mobility of capital and communities competing for enterprise.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Constitutional constraints on government fit his view.

smash-state-machine.rationale: He wants reform through converting legislative chambers.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: He lets each level-1 council choose its own revenue source and permits secession and service substitution, enabling communities to try different arrangements and compete.

sacred-nation.rationale: A sacralized nation is inconsistent with a theory of voluntary association among individual sovereigns.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Theological claim outside his political writing, so neutral.

farm-price-support.rationale: Agricultural price supports are subsidies and protection of the kind he calls economic rents.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He stresses democracy needs consent beyond procedure.

indirect-election.rationale: Each council elects a delegate and alternate to the council above it, up to the legislature and executive.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Foldvary is a Georgist, and his model funds councils from site rents on the view that land value belongs to the community, which is the compensation principle in this statement.

self-ownership.rationale: Foldvary's geolibertarianism pairs equal rights to land with full private rights over one's person and labour.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The model is designed so special-interest campaign money and rent-seeking lose their payoff, which is opposition to special privileges for connected firms.

missingStatements.text: Voters should choose their representatives in groups small enough to meet the candidates in person.
missingStatements.rationale: Face-to-face voting in neighborhood cells is the model's defining remedy for the money and rent-seeking of mass elections.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow design detail of one model; the indirect-election statement captures the structural contrast.

missingStatements.text: Representatives at higher levels of government should be chosen by lower-level councils rather than by mass elections.
missingStatements.rationale: Each council elects a delegate and alternate to the council above it, up to the legislature and executive.

missingStatements.text: A local community should be able to take over a service from a higher level of government and deduct the average cost from what it owes.
missingStatements.rationale: Service substitution lets a level-n council replace a level n+1 service and cut its tax liability, supplementing voice with exit.
missingStatements.declined: Service substitution is a mechanism specific to this model.

notes: The model is theoretical; Foldvary says no complete example exists. Group size varies by source (about 500 to 1,000 residents per cell). Foldvary favors voluntary contractual cells, but the Wikipedia article describes elected councils of a jurisdiction, so adherents differ on how voluntary membership must be.
